newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA FLY IN EUROPEAN PROFESSIONALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA FLY IN EUROPEAN PROFESSIONALS.

text.p: South Africa are flying in several European-based professionals to bolster their team for Wednesday's international against Australia in Johannesburg.

Swiss-based trio Phil Masinga, Sizwe Motaung and David Nyathi arrived on Monday for the match and are to be joined on Tuesday by midfielder John Moshoeu of Turkish club Kocaelispor and Eric Tinkler, who plays for Cagliari in Italy's Serie A.
The match is one of two games scheduled on Wednesday in the Four Nations Cup tournament, which started on Saturday with victories for both teams.
Ghana play Kenya in Wednesday's other match at Johannesburg's recently-built athletics stadium.

All five late arrivals played major roles in South Africa's winning team at the African Nations' Cup finals in February and will bolster an inexperienced squad, who struggled in the closing minutes of Saturday's match against Kenya.
Coach Clive Barker said his team, with six new caps, had been caught out by the pace of international football and had tired in Saturday's game, almost allowing Kenya a late equaliser.
Barker said he would play all five of the foreign-based professionals in the starting line-up on Wednesday against an Australian team without any of their European-based players.
Australian coach Eddie Thomson said he was pleased with his side's performance in their first game, particularly given their lack of match fitness ahead of the start of their domestic soccer season.
"The guys battled in training at first but they've got better all the time," he added.
Ghana were still awaiting confirmation on Monday of the arrival of captain Abedi Pele for their game after he missed the start of the tournament on the weekend.
The former African Footballer of the Year was scheduled to join the Black Stars but missed the trip after finding new employment with German Bundesliga club 1860 Munich.
Their youthful side looked out of their depth in Saturday's opening game and will be hard pressed without Abedi against the robust Kenyans.
The tournament ends on Saturday when South Africa play Ghana and Australia meet Kenya in Pretoria.
